mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a recession and causes equity sell-offs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which typically leads to lower corporate earnings expectations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 1% from prior month
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS (each >1% from prior month) fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high industrial production growth (INDPRO > 120), supply chain bottlenecks ease, leading to lower input costs for firms and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO exceeds 120, the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of such instances over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor force participation rate (PAYEMS growth) indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS growth is positive (above 0.5% MoM) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity, which typically correlates with strong corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO growth is positive (above 0.5% MoM) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 115) signals a contraction in manufacturing, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 115, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances over a 5-year rolling window.
